catalog_quote: L’accento grave serve a indicare dove, come si suol dire, cade l’accento, vale a dire qual è la sillaba pronunciata con maggiore intensità: nella parola pènzanu l’accento cade sulla sillaba pèn-, è cioè quella pronunciata con maggiore intensità. Può anche avere funzione disambiguatrice, per distinguere parole con significati diversi: un esempio è la coppia ḍḍa, ‘quella’, e ḍḍà, ‘là’ ... Le sillabe vengono contate a seconda della loro posizione, partendo dalla fine della parola: ultima, penultima, etc. L’accento grave va sempre rappresentato sulle sillabe accentate diverse dalla penultima, a meno che la parola non termini con uno iato. sweep_summary: Sicilian (sici1248) is in the catalog as 'lexical', decided by the Cademia Siciliana DOS24 v2.2 orthography document (grave accent marks the stressed syllable; minimal pairs such as ḍḍa/ḍḍà). The search of works with stress or accent in the title returned a single item, White, Payne & Mattys (2009), 'Rhythmic and prosodic contrast in Venetan and Sicilian Italian' (John Benjamins, CILT 306, pp. 137-158, DOI 10.1075/cilt.306.07whi). Its abstract (Crossref and the Benjamins landing page, saved to shows it is an acoustic study of speech rhythm, stressed-vowel duration and stress-conditioned vowel reduction in regional Italian spoken by Sicilians, compared with Venetan Italian, not of the Sicilian language, and it says nothing about stress placement. The full text is paywalled with no open copy (OpenAlex closed, no repository full text; Semantic Scholar closed; Bristol/Oxford/York portals 403/404; CORE blocked by an automated-access block), so access is abstract-only; priority for acquisition: none. No new first-hand stress-placement statement was read; the catalog's classification and deciding source stand unchanged. download record appended to (stamp).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is penultimate by default; words stressed elsewhere (antepenultimate, e.g. Sic. víppi, víppimu, víppiru, cádiri, míntere, séntere; or final) are lexically/morphologically given and are marked with an acute accent. This is a citation convention for all southern Italian dialects, not a phonological analysis, but it presupposes the Italian-type system: penultimate default with lexically fixed deviations inside the final three syllables.
new_statements.exceptions: Sicilian class-2 infinitives oscillate between proparoxytonic and paroxytonic types (cádiri/cadíri, míntere/mintíre, séntere/sentíre; p. 259); the preterite of 'drink' has a stressed root alternant víppi/víppimu/víppiru vs vivísti/vivístivu (p. 260); 'be' is rhizotonic throughout (p. 260); §16.3.1.3.2 refers to stressed enclitics in southern dialects (n. 16, p. 258, pointing to §45.3.1).
new_statements.identity_note: Ledgeway 2016 is a survey of all dialects of southern Italy (upper southern dialects and the extreme southern dialects of Sicily, southern Calabria and Salento); the stress convention in footnote 1 is stated for the whole area and the chapter does not single out any particular Sicilian dialect. The Sicilian examples with marked antepenultimate stress are labelled simply 'Sic.'.

tone_statements.quote: Der erste pränukleare Tonhöhenakzent weist nach einem tiefen Zielpunkt zu Produktionsbeginn einen hohen Zielpunkt auf der betonten Silbe von ‚picciottu‘ auf, was einem Tonhöhenakzent L+H* entspricht. ... Die Nuklearkonfiguration für Deklarativsätze mit weitem Fokus ist also H+L* L-L% und kann bei jedem Informanten unabhängig von seinem Herkunftsort beobachtet werden. ... Der Grund hierfür ist die Abhängigkeit des Tonhöhenakzentes von einer betonten Silbe, die in diesem Satztypus am Ende der Äußerung liegt ...
tone_statements.translation: The first prenuclear pitch accent shows, after a low target at the start of the production, a high target on the stressed syllable of 'picciottu', which corresponds to a pitch accent L+H*. ... The nuclear configuration for broad-focus declaratives is thus H+L* L-L% and can be observed in every informant regardless of place of origin. ... The reason for this is the dependence of the pitch accent on a stressed syllable, which in this sentence type lies at the end of the utterance ...

tone.quote: podemos concluir que existen dos grandes grupos diferenciados por la entonación de las interrogativas absolutas. [...] agrupamos las variedades que presentan un tonema con tono ascendente en el núcleo y descendente en la cola: Alcamo, Caltanissetta, Castelbuono, Marsala, Mazara del Vallo, Modica, Palermo, Piana degli Albanesi, Serradifalco, Siracusa, Termini Imerese y Trapani. [...] El segundo gran grupo coincide con la mayoría de las variedades orientales: Caltagirone, Catania, Enna, Lentini y Paternò. En estos puntos de encuesta se producen un tono descendente en el núcleo y ascendente en la cola de las interrogativas absolutas independientemente de la estructura acentual del tonema.
tone.locator: p. 150, cap. V §2 'Primeras conclusiones del análisis acústico de los dialectos sicilianos'; ToBI table pp. 153-154
tone.translation: we can conclude that there are two large groups distinguished by the intonation of yes-no questions. [...] we group the varieties that show a nuclear configuration with a rising tone on the nucleus and a falling tone on the tail: Alcamo, Caltanissetta, Castelbuono, Marsala, Mazara del Vallo, Modica, Palermo, Piana degli Albanesi, Serradifalco, Siracusa, Termini Imerese and Trapani. [...] The second large group coincides with most of the eastern varieties: Caltagirone, Catania, Enna, Lentini and Paternò. At these survey points a falling tone is produced on the nucleus and a rising tone on the tail of yes-no questions regardless of the stress pattern of the final word.

tone.quote: Since the intonation system(s) of Sicily has/have not been exhaustively explored except for some regional varieties of Italian (see [7], [9], [10]), the present study aims at giving a first overview of the potential prosodic patterns found in this area [...]. For the first experiment we analysed the prosodic contours of each sample and grouped them according to their final prosodic scheme. Four main contours were found: rising-falling, aligned with the nuclear vowel or delayed (Fig. 1 and 2), total falling (Fig. 3) or falling-rising (Fig. 4).
